items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Bill Challis at the time, his arrangements were quite different from Gene Gifford's. What he did, I liked much better, you know.

ctx.x: What about a few other arrangers we can mention -- certainly Don Redman was a very important figure, but what about some of the white bands and some of the white arrangers for the Goldkette Gold-Keg band, for example?
Well, I think that the only one I -- the only two I remember, Gene Gifford and outstandingly, I might say, Bill Challis.
Uh huh. Now just in general, how could you describe their style in general? Or something
